twisted_product: D=lambda_(minus1)(N); x star y=xyD on the additive group A.

unitization.derivation: Expand(n1+i(x))(n-prime1+i(x-prime)); use1 as identity and i(x)i(x-prime)=i(xx-prime D). This proves the exact second A-coordinate x-prime in5.5.2.
unitization.printed_y_test: At A=Z,N=0,n=n-prime=0,x=1,x-prime=0,y=1, the source final y gives(0,1), whereas multiplication by(0,0) gives(0,0).

constant_term.identity: The p=0 term is the adjoined unit(1,0), not an element i(a) of the augmentation ideal.
constant_term.additivity: For p>=1 the coefficient of H_x H_y is i(lambda^p(N,x)+lambda^p(N,y)+sum_{i+j=p,i,j>0}lambda^i(N,x)lambda^j(N,y)D). Formula5.4.1 identifies this with i(lambda^p(N,x+y)), and the constant coefficient remains(1,0). Thus H_x H_y=H_(x+y).
constant_term.first_coefficient: The positive definition gives lambda^1(N,x)=x by cancellation of D in the universal polynomial ring and substitution, hence the first coefficient of lambda_t(n,x) is(n,x).
constant_term.scope: 5.3.1 is retained only for p>=1 as printed. No inverse of D or value in A for its p=0 division expression is introduced.

unit_prose_issue.example: A=Z,N=0,d=1 yields D=1 and the ordinary unital product.
unit_prose_issue.product_check: The second coordinate of Phi((n,x)(m,y)) is nm+ny+mx+xy=(n+x)(m+y); the first is nm.
unit_prose_issue.scope: The source phrase asserting absence of a unit fails for this allowed instance; the displayed unitization is nonetheless verified by Phi. Source prose is retained with the exact example recorded.
